newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds fall in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds fall in thin trade.

text.p: Argentine bonds finished lower Wednesday, as the market broke a string of firmer closes as declines in U.S. Treasuries pulled the market lower.
"The market needed some profit-taking and it is good for the market to consolidate before rising again," said an analyst. The yield on the U.S. 30-year bond rose three basis points to 6.40 percent.
Activity was thin again, however, testifying to the fact that investors left their positions intact, added the analyst.
The dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 fell 0.05 to 122.25. Argentina's FRB due 2005 slipped 1/8 to 86-6/8.
